newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel urges SPD to back tax reforms.
newsitem.headline: Waigel urges SPD to back tax reforms.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel on Tuesday urged the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) to drop their blockade of government tax reforms and help restore national economic fortunes.
"You have sacrificed the common good on the altar of party tactics," Waigel charged in a debate in the Bundestag lower house of parliament on tax reforms.

The Bundestag interrupted its summer recess to debate Waigel's plan to slash 30 billion marks ($16.1 billion) in income and corporate taxes, which were blocked last week by the SPD majority in parliament's mediation committee.
Waigel attacked SPD leader Oskar Lafontaine for vetoing government tax reforms, while promising that his own party would introduce its own reforms if it wins the September 1998 general election.
"That is an evil strategy, we need the reforms now for jobs, investment and the economy," Waigel said.
Waigel said the blockade of reform would hurt both sides of the political divide in Germany, and said the government was ready to give ground to reach a deal.
"We are ready to compromise, but do not want an unworthy compromise," Waigel said. "We need a reform to prevent further erosion and put tax revenues on a sound basis."

Chancellor Helmut Kohl's slim Bundestag majority was expected to vote to initiate a second round of parliamentary mediation on the tax reform. It was also set to rubber-stamp a cross-party deal reached last week in mediation to scrap a capital trading tax on companies. ($ = 1.863 German Marks)
